_comment: Subsector summaries for the <SubsectorHero /> card that sits above /market-map results when a single subsector filter is active, and the header block on /sectors/[slug]. Keyed by `toSlug(subsector_name)`. Omit a subsector to disable the hero — the grid falls back to its default empty state. Keep prose tight (2-3 sentences max) so the hero doesn't push the grid below the fold.

centralized-stablecoins.name: Centralized Stablecoins
centralized-stablecoins.what: Fiat-backed dollars issued by a centralized entity that holds reserves off-chain (USDC, USDT, PYUSD, and so on).
centralized-stablecoins.why: Still the plumbing for the vast majority of on-chain dollar flow. Reserve composition, attestation cadence, and issuer jurisdiction are the risk vectors that matter.
centralized-stablecoins.trust_model: Issuer custody + attestation / audit; regulated banking rails for mint and redeem.

decentralized-stablecoins.name: Decentralized Stablecoins
decentralized-stablecoins.what: Stablecoins backed by on-chain collateral (DAI, LUSD, crvUSD, …) with protocol-enforced liquidation and redemption mechanics.
decentralized-stablecoins.why: The canonical hedge against issuer risk. Trade-offs live between capital efficiency, peg robustness, and the collateral mix.
decentralized-stablecoins.trust_model: Smart-contract-enforced over-collateralisation; governance controls parameters and collateral admission.

synthetic-and-yield-bearing-dollars.name: Synthetic & Yield-Bearing Dollars
synthetic-and-yield-bearing-dollars.what: Delta-neutral and basis-trade tokens (USDe, sUSDe, yield-bearing variants) that combine stable exposure with native yield.
synthetic-and-yield-bearing-dollars.why: Fastest-growing corner of the stablecoin stack. Understand the trade mechanics, unwind path, and redemption queue before sizing up.
synthetic-and-yield-bearing-dollars.trust_model: Hedged exposure via perp / basis trade; relies on CEX custody, funding-rate regime, and collateral liquidity.

global-on-ramps.name: Global On-Ramps
global-on-ramps.what: Payment-method-to-crypto bridges (Stripe, MoonPay, Transak, Ramp, …) that convert cards, bank transfers, and mobile money into stablecoins.
global-on-ramps.why: First-mile user experience. Coverage, fees, and KYC depth vary drastically by corridor.
global-on-ramps.trust_model: Licensed money-services businesses; FX and settlement risk sits with the operator.

institutional-payment-rails.name: Institutional Payment Rails
institutional-payment-rails.what: B2B settlement networks for large-ticket stablecoin flow (Fireblocks Network, Visa, Mastercard Crypto Credential, bank tokenisation pilots).
institutional-payment-rails.why: Where corporate treasury and cross-border B2B is actually moving. Throughput and compliance tooling separate credible entrants from press-release plays.
institutional-payment-rails.trust_model: Regulated institutional custodians + permissioned networks; KYB / AML enforced at the edge.

regional-payment-networks.name: Regional Payment Networks
regional-payment-networks.what: Local-currency rails using stablecoins under the hood (LatAm, SEA, Africa). Often bundled with off-ramps and payroll tooling.
regional-payment-networks.why: The clearest product-market fit for stablecoins today. Corridor economics and cash-out partners drive volumes.
regional-payment-networks.trust_model: Regional MSB/PSP licensing; stablecoin leg introduces issuer + bridge risk.

lending-markets.name: Lending Markets
lending-markets.what: Over-collateralised lending protocols (Aave, Compound, Morpho, Spark) that let users borrow against on-chain collateral.
lending-markets.why: The backbone of DeFi leverage and yield. Understanding IRM shape, oracle choice, and collateral factors is table stakes.

dex-and-liquidity-pools.name: DEX & Liquidity Pools
dex-and-liquidity-pools.what: Automated market makers and order-book DEXs (Uniswap, Curve, Balancer, dYdX, …) where price discovery and routing happen on-chain.
dex-and-liquidity-pools.why: Controls execution quality for every DeFi app downstream. AMM shape and MEV exposure drive returns for LPs and searchers.

liquid-staking-tokens.name: Liquid Staking Tokens
liquid-staking-tokens.what: Tokenised ETH staking positions (stETH, rETH, cbETH, sfrxETH, …) issued by staking pools or providers.
liquid-staking-tokens.why: The largest DeFi asset category. Validator-set decentralisation, slashing insurance, and peg resilience decide winners.
liquid-staking-tokens.trust_model: Operator trust + smart-contract custody; peg maintained via redemption / LST secondary markets.

restaking-systems.name: Restaking Systems
restaking-systems.what: Protocols (EigenLayer, Symbiotic, Karak, …) that let staked ETH or LSTs opt in to securing additional services (AVSs).
restaking-systems.why: Rapidly expanding shared-security primitive. Slashing conditions per AVS and operator-set quality are the live risks.
restaking-systems.trust_model: Stake-based cryptoeconomic security with opt-in slashing; still maturing.
